\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{استعداد} (este'dâd)}{استعداد (este'dâd)}]{\fa{استعداد} (este'dâd) — talent, aptitude}

\label{lesson:FA-C527-estedad}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to design, then the Persian for to create.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{استعداد}}
\textbf{\fa{استعداد}} (\emph{este'dâd}) — \textquotedblleft{}talent, aptitude\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{او} \fa{در} \fa{موسیقی} \fa{استعداد} \fa{زیادی} \fa{دارد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{u dar musiqi este'dâd-e ziyâdi dârad.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
He has a great talent for music.
\end{quote}

\emph{dar chizi este'dâd dâshtan} — to have a gift for something.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{este'dâd} is a loan, usually traced to Arabic \emph{istiʿdād}, 'readiness, aptitude'. EtymDB has no entry for it.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{este'dâd}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{este'dâd}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{este'dâd}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for to design, then the Persian for to create, then say \emph{este'dâd} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \fa{استعداد} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Talent, aptitude\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{خلاقیت} (khallâqiyat)}{خلاقیت (khallâqiyat)}]{\fa{خلاقیت} (khallâqiyat) — creativity}

\label{lesson:FA-C527-khallaqiyat}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to create, then the Persian for talent.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{خلاقیت}}
\textbf{\fa{خلاقیت}} (\emph{khallâqiyat}) — \textquotedblleft{}creativity\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{این} \fa{کار} \fa{خلاقیت} \fa{زیادی} \fa{میخواهد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{in kâr khallâqiyat-e ziyâdi mikhâhad.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
This work takes a lot of creativity.
\end{quote}

Built on \emph{khallâq} 'creative'.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{khallâqiyat} is built in Persian on \emph{khallâq}, 'creative', a loan usually traced to Arabic \emph{ḫallāq}, 'creator', with an abstract ending. EtymDB has no entry for it.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{شاهکار} (shâhkâr)}{شاهکار (shâhkâr)}]{\fa{شاهکار} (shâhkâr) — a masterpiece}

\label{lesson:FA-C527-shahkar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for talent, then the Persian for creativity.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{شاهکار}}
\textbf{\fa{شاهکار}} (\emph{shâhkâr}) — \textquotedblleft{}a masterpiece\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{این} \fa{نقاشی} \fa{شاهکار} \fa{اوست}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{in naqqâshi shâhkâr-e ust.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
This painting is his masterpiece.
\end{quote}

\emph{shâh} 'king' + \emph{kâr} 'work': the king of works.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{shâhkâr} is built on two inherited words: \emph{shâh}, 'king', and \emph{kâr}, 'work', both of which EtymDB traces to Middle Persian (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{رقصنده} (raqsande)}{رقصنده (raqsande)}]{\fa{رقصنده} (raqsande) — a dancer}

\label{lesson:FA-C527-raqsande}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for creativity, then the Persian for a masterpiece.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{رقصنده}}
\textbf{\fa{رقصنده}} (\emph{raqsande}) — \textquotedblleft{}a dancer\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{رقصنده} \fa{ها} \fa{با} \fa{لباس} \fa{محلی} \fa{روی} \fa{صحنه} \fa{آمدند}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{raqsandehâ bâ lebâs-e mahalli ru-ye sahne âmadand.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The dancers came on stage in local dress.
\end{quote}

From \emph{raqsidan} 'to dance' (stem \emph{raqs-}) + \emph{-ande} 'one who'.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{raqsande} is built in Persian on \emph{raqs}, 'dance', a loan usually traced to Arabic \emph{raqṣ}, with the native ending \emph{-ande}, 'one who'.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{تحسین} \fa{کردن} (tahsin kardan)}{تحسین کردن (tahsin kardan)}]{\fa{تحسین} \fa{کردن} (tahsin kardan) — to admire, to praise}

\label{lesson:FA-C527-tahsin-kardan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a masterpiece, then the Persian for a dancer.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{تحسین} \fa{کردن}}
\textbf{\fa{تحسین} \fa{کردن}} (\emph{tahsin kardan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to admire, to praise\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{همه} \fa{کار} \fa{او} \fa{را} \fa{تحسین} \fa{کردند}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{hame kâr-e u râ tahsin kardand.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Everyone admired her work.
\end{quote}

\emph{tahsin} 'admiration, praise' + \emph{kardan}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{tahsin} is a loan, usually traced to Arabic \emph{taḥsīn}, 'finding something beautiful, praising'. EtymDB has no entry for it. \emph{kardan} is inherited Persian.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tahsin kardan}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{tahsin kardan}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for a masterpiece, then the Persian for a dancer, then say \emph{tahsin kardan} again
\end{itemize}

\section[(dialogue)]{Words from chapters 520–527 — a review}

\label{lesson:FA-R527-review-520-527}



\begin{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}

  \item a theatre, a stage, a play, a spectator, a role

(\textbf{\fa{شعر}}.) A poet? (\textbf{\fa{شاعر}}.) A ghazal? (\textbf{\fa{غزل}}.) A quatrain? (\textbf{\fa{رباعی}}.) A couplet? (\textbf{\fa{بیت}}.) A rhyme? (\textbf{\fa{قافیه}}.) To compose? (\textbf{\fa{فیلمنامه}}.) A cameraman? (\textbf{\fa{فیلمبردار}}.) To play a role? (\textbf{\fa{نقش} \fa{بازی} \fa{کردن}}.) An actor? (\textbf{\fa{هنرپیشه}}.) A painter? (\textbf{\fa{نقاش}}.) A canvas? (\textbf{\fa{بوم}}.) A paintbrush? (\textbf{\fa{قلم} \fa{مو}}.) Watercolour? (\textbf{\fa{آبرنگ}}.) A gallery? (\textbf{\fa{گالری}}.) A sculptor? (\textbf{\fa{مجسمه} \fa{ساز}}.)
